component.name: Napkin
component.summary: A persistent scratch surface for your computer

description.p: Napkin is somewhere to put things before you know whether they matter. Paste text and images into it; nothing needs a name, a folder or a tag.
Everything stays on this machine. There is no account, no sync and no network access of any kind. What you paste is written to a local database that only you can read.
Napkin holds two kinds of thing and no others:

ul.li: Text, including links, which render as a chip you can open
Images, pasted from anywhere — PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG and animated GIF

description.p: Nothing is deleted on your behalf. Napkins you have not touched in a while move to an "Older" section rather than disappearing, and only the trash empties — of what you already deleted. Everything can be exported to a folder of ordinary files at any time.
Napkin can work out the sums you write on it.

ul.li: End a line with = and press Ctrl+Tab: "rent 1200*12 =" becomes "rent 1200*12 = 14400". Calculate is also in the right-click menu while editing.
Change a number and press Ctrl+Tab again to recalculate. Select several lines to fill in every line that ends in =.
Percentages work as on a calculator, and amounts in $, €, £, ¥ or ₹ keep their symbol and their 1,234,567 or 12,34,567 grouping.
The answer is ordinary text, and nothing is calculated unless you ask. A line that is not a sum is left alone.

description.p: Napkin opens on a board rather than on a single column of notes.

ul.li: The window now opens wide enough for two columns of cards. It can still be made narrower; it just no longer starts that way.

description.p: Napkin now says when it has done something, and several keyboard actions that quietly did the wrong thing were corrected.

ul.li: Copying says "Copied" however you ask for it, not only from the button on the card.
Ctrl+A selects the whole napkin. On a long one it used to select only the cards on screen, so Ctrl+A then Delete could leave most of them behind.
Arrow keys move the way the board looks: up and down stay in a column, left and right cross to the next one.
Quit quits, including from the tray with the window already hidden.
The tray's "Paste onto a new napkin" works instead of leaving an empty napkin behind.
Pasting something Napkin cannot hold now says so rather than doing nothing.
A copy that cannot be made says so, and cutting a picture whose file is missing no longer deletes it.

description.p: Napkin follows the desktop switching between light and dark while it is running, without a restart.
On Windows, dark mode now reaches buttons, dropdowns, text fields and scroll bars; they used to stay light.
The Linux AppImage now starts on Wayland desktops; 0.1.1's crashed on KDE Plasma under Wayland.
First published release, and the first for Windows.

ul.li: A Windows build: a zip that runs without installing anything.
Search works on older SQLite; the v0.1.0 build failed there and was never published.
Deleted items go to the trash and can be restored; Ctrl+Z undoes the last action.
Typing anywhere starts a note; Pin and Keep are Ctrl+P and Ctrl+D.
A new icon, toolbar icons, and a Settings button.
Exported notes keep their line endings exactly as typed.
